thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 detected — cross-region routing anomalies from eu-west -> us-central. Error spike and elevated p99 latency since 05:12 UTC. Auto-paging oncall.

jen-ozaki: getting reports from support about pages and slow customer calls. Dashboard shows sudden drop in eu-west capacity and a cascade of requests being sent to us-central. Suspect region pinning mis-evaluation after AZ ejection. @arnold-oncall you were paged, can you ack?

arnold-oncall: acked. I’m on it. seeing traffic skew to us-central ~90% from eu-west origins. Latency p99 jumped from 120ms -> 950ms for some embeddings calls.

omar-khan: checking routing-policy decision logs. There are a bunch of policy-eval failures where region affinity check returned empty and fallback selected cost-based route that points to us-central. Looks like a stale health signal from eu-west healthprober.

sasha-chen: I’m pulling the healthprober logs now. There’s an AZ-level NACL flap in eu-west-2a that caused ~30% of prober probes to fail starting 05:08 UTC. Health aggregator marked region unhealthy intermittently, then healed, then flapped again — timing matches the policy churn.

mike-sre: timeline wise: prober flap -> policy thought eu-west degraded -> routing pins cleared -> many sessions re-resolved and routed to us-central -> client connections saw higher latency. Repeated churn created a routing loop for some sticky sessions.

jen-ozaki: important: customer impact = sessionized traffic and long-running websocket/chat flows dropped or reconnected to other regions, causing visible UX blips. Linda, any high-priority customer reports?

linda-cs: Support has 4 high-priority tickets (2 enterprise) reporting slow responses and reconnects. One customer in fintech reported timeouts during trades (escalated). I’ll flag legal/regulatory owners for fintech account.

arnold-oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause routing policy rollouts that are active, 2) force-pin eu-west for existing sessions, 3) reduce DNS TTL for ingress to 30s to limit prolonged misresolutions, 4) coordinate with cloud for AZ-level network fix.

tina-eng: I can push a pin override. Suggest runbook step: write-mode override to stickiness table for eu-west for 15m. Command:

```bash
# CLI to set stickiness override for eu-west for 15 minutes
redwoodctl routing stickiness set --region eu-west --dur 15m --reason "incident 1765432100: AZ flap"
```

arnold-oncall: do it. @tina-eng please proceed and confirm. Also set TTL to 30s at the edge config:

```bash
# edgectl example
edgectl config set --route default --dns-ttl 30s
```

tina-eng: override applied. Confirmed active sticks count increased, policy evals now short-circuited to eu-west for new decisions.

deploy-bot: config change deployed: edge.dns.ttl=30s by tina-eng at 05:28 UTC.

omar-khan: routing policy rollout paused (id: rollout-2026-03-15-42). Stopped new changes for the next 1h.

sasha-chen: cloud says they see NACL flaps — they applied a temporary NACL allow rule to stabilize control plane traffic in eu-west-2a. They've scheduled a deeper investigation but immediate connectivity is improving.

mike-sre: monitoring: p99 latency now trending down from 950ms -> 320ms within 6 minutes of stickiness override. Error rate also reducing. Keep an eye on reconnect storms.

jen-ozaki: good. Start a 15-minute customer-facing status update draft. Linda can you help with messaging and which customers to call directly?

linda-cs: already on it. Prioritizing fintech enterprise and two PLG customers with high request rates. Draft ready, will post once we confirm stabilization for 10m.

arnold-oncall: handoff plan: I’ll stay on for next 30m and then hand to @mike-sre for monitoring and next steps. We need postmortem owner — @tina-eng can you take lead on root cause analysis for the stickiness/policy interaction?

tina-eng: I’ll own RCA. I’ll collect policy-eval traces, prober telemetry, and rollout timeline. Plan to surface findings in postmortem within 48h.

mike-sre: taking over monitoring at 05:40 UTC. I’ll annotate dashboards and keep an eye on reconnect counts and per-customer tail latency. If anything regresses, I’ll re-escalate.

jen-ozaki: notes for post-incident: potential gaps — healthprober debounce too sensitive to AZ-level transient errors, routing-policy fallback aggressive, and stickiness reconciliation didn't protect long-lived sessions. Include suggested mitigations in RCA: prober smoothing, fallback hysteresis, and fail-open sticky behavior.

arnold-oncall: confirmed stabilization for now. Incident severity remains P1 until we declare recovered. Next update in 10m or sooner on any regression.

incident-bot: Update: P1 status — mitigation in progress, acknowledgement by arnold-oncall, engaged cloud provider.

mike-sre: status @ 05:40 UTC — metrics stable for 12m, p99 ~ 300ms, error rate back to baseline for the majority of routes. Still monitoring.

linda-cs: customer messaging posted to status page and outreach started. Two customers acknowledged and are monitoring.

arnold-oncall: handing off active watch to mike-sre at 05:50 UTC. I’m available if needed.

mike-sre: accepted handoff. Will keep thread updated.

jen-ozaki: thanks all — please keep notes for RCA and attach logs: /var/logs/routing-policy/1765432100/*. Also capture prober metrics and cloud NACL change ID.

sasha-chen: adding prober trace links and policy-eval traces to the incident folder.

mike-sre: last check 05:59 UTC — no regression in last 19m. Marking incident as mitigated; will transition to postmortem and customer follow-ups.

incident-bot: P1 mitigated — monitoring phase. Postmortem owner: tina-eng.

jen-ozaki: closing notes: impact window ~05:08–05:40 UTC. Primary cause: AZ-level control-plane flapping that cascaded into sticky-session churn via routing policy fallback. Postmortem to include timelines, mitigations implemented, and recommended config changes.
